renders.note: python has no element node; a template is a string literal and the nearest construct that produces an object from a name is a CALL, published as `calls`

mixes_in.note: python's ONE superclass clause: `class C(A, B)` — every base is published as `extends`, and the source cannot say which base is the mixin

part_of.note: python's unit of inclusion is an IMPORT, published as `imports`

renders.construct: python's nearest 'a thing that renders another thing' is the TEMPLATE — a string that carries placeholders, and the call that renders it. python has no COMPONENT and no ELEMENT LITERAL.
renders.missingDiscriminator: the relation is between a COMPONENT and the component it renders; python has no component type and no element literal, so there is no node type that could carry the relation — only a template string and a call.
renders.alreadyPublishedUnder: calls (the RENDER CALL is a call); the component-to-component relation has NO carrier, and a template's placeholders are published under NO label

mixes_in.construct: python's MULTIPLE-INHERITANCE class statement `class C(A, B)` — one class, several bases merged into one supertype chain. The near-miss is not the spelling; it is the MERGE.
mixes_in.missingDiscriminator: python has NO syntax that separates 'the base' from 'the composed member': every base in `class C(A, B)` is a NOMINAL SUPERTYPE (python's MRO makes `issubclass(C, B)` true), so a `mixes_in` edge would have to name a member that IS a supertype — which is the `extends` edge the analyzer already publishes.
mixes_in.mergingPairsExample: class ApiResponse(BaseModel, Generic[T]) → the pair (ApiResponse, Generic[T])

part_of.construct: python's UNIT OF INCLUSION is the IMPORT — `import a.b` pulls another module's source into the program. The near-miss is the construct that INCLUDES another unit.
part_of.missingDiscriminator: a Dart `part` SHARES the library's single scope; a python import CREATES binding scope and names a module — the two are different relations, and python's grammar has no node type that can express the shared-scope one.
